title: Routing deployment heuristics and linting manual
content:
Purpose

This working manual collects pragmatic heuristics, lint rules, and a compact set of schema examples for routing rule configuration and progressive rollout mechanics. It is intended for engineers authoring control-plane route manifests and for automation that validates, schedules, and gates canary deployments across regions and capacity tiers. The goal is to reduce on-call risk, avoid subtle routing regressions, and encode operational best-practices in the linter/CI checks.

High-level principles

- Explicit compatibility: every routing rule must declare model compatibility (model_family, version_range, quantization_profile). Avoid implicit fallbacks in rule blobs.
- Telemetry-first gating: use latency, p50/p95, downstream error rate, and end-to-end correctness traces (when available) as primary gates. Cost and throughput are secondary but tracked.
- Conservative defaults: short canaries with small traffic weight, automated rollback on exceeded thresholds, and automatic throttling of rollout growth when noisy signals are detected.
- Idempotent rollouts: automation should be able to resume partially-applied rollouts safely. Keep manifest atoms small (route, selector, matrix).

Compact routing-rule schema (recommended JSON form)

Example rule (authoring reference):

{
  "id": "route-svc-embed-prod-2026-03",
  "description": "Route embeddings requests to embedder-v3 in us-west with regional fallback",
  "selector": {
    "path": "/v1/embeddings",
    "model_family": "embedder",
    "client_tier": ["standard", "partner"]
  },
  "targets": [
    {
      "name": "embedder-v3-quant",
      "model": "embedder/v3",
      "version": "3.2.0",
      "region": "us-west1",
      "capacity_tier": "dedicated",
      "quant_profile": "q4_0",
      "weight": 100
    }
  ],
  "rollout": {
    "strategy": "staggered",
    "canary": {
      "initial_pct": 2,
      "growth_schedule": [2, 5, 15, 40, 100],
      "per_step_min_duration": "7m",
      "concurrent_steps": 1
    },
    "gating": {
      "metrics": ["latency_p95_ms", "err_rate", "model_quality_regressions"],
      "thresholds": {
        "latency_p95_ms": 400,
        "err_rate": 0.003,
        "model_quality_regressions": 0.01
      },
      "evaluation_window": "5m",
      "consecutive_fails_to_abort": 2
    }
  },
  "metadata": {
    "owner": "eng-platform",
    "jira": "PLAT-987",
    "created_by": "ava.chen@redwood.ai"
  }
}

Notes on fields:

- selector: lightweight matching predicate; prefer path + model_family over client IP ranges for portability.
- targets: keep each target small and declarative. Weight is relative; sum may be less than or equal to 100 with rollout filling the remainder.
- rollout.strategy: allowed values ["instant", "staggered", "blue_green"]. We recommend "staggered" for model swaps and behind-the-scenes kernel changes.
- rollout.canary.growth_schedule: absolute percentages; automation enforces monotonicity.
- gating.metrics: automation understands platform-standard metric names (latency_p95_ms, latency_p50_ms, err_rate, token_cost_per_request, model_quality_regressions). Custom metrics must be mapped in telemetry config.

Validation/lint rules (what the validator enforces)

1) Schema validation
   - required top-level fields: id, selector, targets, rollout.
   - targets must include name, model, version, region or region_alias, capacity_tier.

2) Sanity checks
   - initial_pct > 0 and <= 10 for any canary unless strategy == "instant".
   - growth_schedule elements must be strictly increasing and end at 100. If not, the validator warns.
   - per_step_min_duration >= 1m and <= 24h.

3) Safety gates
   - If target.capacity_tier == "dedicated" and selector.client_tier includes "partner", require explicit SLO escalation and owner tag.
   - Cross-region target lists are allowed but must include a primary_region flag. Multi-region failover routes must have a cooldown window and circuit-breaker thresholds.

4) Telemetry requirements
   - Any rollout that changes model_family must include at least one correctness metric in gating.metrics (e.g., model_quality_regressions or a labeled eval-set mismatch metric).
   - If rollout affects production embeddings or reranking endpoints, require a baseline evaluation trace id in metadata.

5) Lint heuristics (warnings, not hard errors)
   - Missing description -> warn.
   - selectors that match all paths (e.g., path: "/") -> warn with suggested narrower patterns.
   - Targets that pin to a single node identifier -> error unless explicitly allowed by team policy.

Automated rollout state machine (summary)

States: VALIDATED -> SCHEDULED -> CANARY_RUNNING -> GATED_ROLLUP -> ROLLOUT_COMPLETE | ROLLBACK_INITIATED | ABORTED

Key invariants:
- Only one active rollout per selector model_family + region per tenant to avoid traffic races.
- Rollouts are checkpointed in the control-plane DB every step; steps are idempotent and resume on controller restart.
- Each step records telemetry snapshots: pre-step baseline (5m) and post-step observation (evaluation_window).

Gating logic (high-level pseudocode)

if observed.metric[latency_p95_ms] > gate.thresholds.latency_p95_ms * 1.05 for evaluation_window:
  increment failure_count
else:
  reset failure_count

if failure_count >= gating.consecutive_fails_to_abort:
  abort rollout -> ROLLBACK_INITIATED
elif observed.regression_count > gating.thresholds.model_quality_regressions:
  pause rollout and create manual-review ticket
else:
  proceed to next scheduled percent

Rollback semantics

- soft_rollback: reduce canary weight to previous healthy step and run extended observation (30m). Used for transient spikes.
- hard_rollback: immediate revert to previous target(s) and create incident. Triggered on latent severe errors (err_rate spikes above 5x baseline or p99 catastrophic increases).
- Rollbacks are recorded as explicit mutations in the control plane (immutable audit line). Automation always records the reason and snapshot ids.

Multi-region considerations

- Regional awareness: when targeting multiple regions, treat each region rollout as a separate rollup group unless the change touches global routing metadata (e.g., model_family rename).
- Stagger across regions: prefer non-overlapping schedules for large changes (e.g., us-east -> us-west -> eu-west). If simultaneous cross-region change is needed, require an SRE signoff.
- Cross-region fallback: ensure requests routed to fallback region carry a routed_region header for tracing and cost accounting.

Operational checklist before authoring a rollout manifest

- [ ] Has a clear owner and on-call contact.
- [ ] Baseline telemetry snapshot captured and linked in metadata.
- [ ] Eval set ID (if model quality is impacted) included.
- [ ] Jira ticket referenced.
- [ ] Linter passes locally and in CI with no errors; warnings are acknowledged.
- [ ] Automated rollback policy present and not disabled.

Developer notes and examples

- Use the CLI tool `rw-route lint <manifest>` to run the schema validator. Pass `--strict` in urgent/enterprise contexts.
- For quick swaps where model architecture is identical (hotfix PRs), `strategy: instant` may be used but requires a previous approval label and an extended post-deploy watch.
- When authoring fallbacks, prefer explicit target ordering plus health_check endpoints in target metadata so the control plane can triage degraded capacities quickly.

Open questions and future work (short list)

- Entropy-based scheduling: use request distribution entropy to pick seed users for canaries rather than fixed percent. Prototype exists but needs reliability benchmarks.
- Cost-aware rollout: integrate token-cost-per-request into gating so a model that increases latency but reduces cost can be weighed properly.
- Granular per-client quotas during canary: allow partner clients to opt-in to early canary traffic for dogs-in-the-field tests.

Appendix: quick lint rules cheat sheet

- ERROR if targets[] missing model/version/name/region.
- ERROR if rollout.strategy == "instant" and gating.metrics missing.
- WARN if selector.path == "/".
- WARN if canary.initial_pct > 10.
- ERROR if growth_schedule not monotonic or final != 100.
- WARN if metadata.owner absent.

Owner: Ava Chen (eng-platform)
Contact: ava.chen@redwood.ai

This is a living document. Update the validator if the linting rules are too noisy; we prefer failing fast in CI but want manageable developer experience.
